review_kind: AI-assisted source and identity-scope review; no human receipt
scope: A bounded source guide, not a resolved inventory of Chiricahua governments or Mexican communities

public_notes.text: For the history of families who remained near Fort Sill, start with the Tribe's own account of release and resettlement in 1914. Mescalero's account provides a separate history of Chiricahua arrivals there. The related records remain separate.
Mescalero records Chiricahua families arriving in 1913. Fort Sill's own history describes families who remained in Oklahoma. Related ancestry does not make the present governments interchangeable.

official_resources.label: Fort Sill Apache history in the Tribe's own words
official_resources.purpose: A starting point for imprisonment, displacement, resettlement and the Tribe's efforts to regain a land base. Historical events are dated accounts, not a statement of present land boundaries.

official_resources.label: Mescalero Apache tribal history
official_resources.purpose: The Tribe's own account of Mescalero, Lipan and Chiricahua people within its community. Begin with Tribal History and Reservation History. This site does not reproduce ceremonial instructions.

official_resources.label: Chiricahua Apache Nation's own governance account
official_resources.purpose: This named community describes its councils. Its account does not establish federal recognition, exclusive representation of all Chiricahua people or the legal status of other communities.

official_resources.label: Mexico: INPI's broader N’dee o N’nee o Ndé entry
official_resources.purpose: INPI describes contemporary communities in Chihuahua, Sonora and Coahuila. This is a broader people-level account, not a list of Chiricahua governments or proof that any named US community represents them. Mexican communities' own names and governing bodies still need separate research.

official_resources.label: Mexico: INPI's broader N’dee o N’nee o Ndé entry
official_resources.purpose: A broader people-level account in Mexico. It must not be treated as a synonym for this Tribal government or an exclusively Chiricahua category. Mexican communities' own names and governing bodies still need separate research.

official_resources.label: Mexico: INPI's broader N’dee o N’nee o Ndé entry
official_resources.purpose: A broader people-level account in Mexico. It does not establish that this named US community represents those communities. Mexican communities' own names and governing bodies still need separate research.
